source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 30. Exercises reused from the lesson.
topic: Twelve months that follow the moon

learn.en: The Islamic year follows the moon. Each new moon begins a new month, and there are twelve months.
learn.title: Following the moon

learn.en: A month has 29 or 30 days — never 31!
learn.title: 29 or 30 days

learn.en: The months: Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, Rabi' ath-Thani, Jumada al-Ula, Jumada ath-Thaniyah, Rajab, Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah and Dhul-Hijjah.
learn.title: Twelve months

learn.en: The Prophet ﷺ was born in Rabi' al-Awwal. We fast in Ramadan, celebrate Eid al-Fitr in Shawwal and Eid al-Adha in Dhul-Hijjah.
learn.title: Special months

learn.en: “Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve lunar months in the register of Allah.” (Qur'an 9:36)
learn.title: From the Qur'an

learn.en: Jazakum Allahu khayran — you have finished Islamic Studies Level 2! 🌙
learn.title: Well done!

order.en: Put the Islamic months in order

quiz.en: True or false? The Islamic year follows the changes of the moon.
True or false? Each new moon begins a new year.
True or false? Some Islamic months have 31 days.
True or false? August is an Islamic month.
Which is the first month of the Islamic calendar?
In which month do Muslims fast?

think.q: What is today's Islamic date? Can you find it with Mum or Dad?
think.a: Look it up together — and watch for the new moon at the end of the month!

parents.summary: The Hijri calendar: twelve lunar months of 29 or 30 days, Muharram to Dhul-Hijjah; Ramadan for fasting, Eids in Shawwal and Dhul-Hijjah.
parents.tip: Go moon-spotting together at the start of the next Islamic month.
